This is a clear breach of their [Seller Performance Policy](https://sellercentral.amazon.com/gp/help/help.html?itemID=200500650) (specifically, **Section 1.2: Review Manipulation**). 2. **Deceptive Practices** – The seller is misleading buyers into thinking they’ve left a review when they haven’t, which is unethical and could harm other customers’ trust. 3. **Pattern of Behavior** – The fact that they have 100% positive ratings (likely due to this scheme) suggests systemic manipulation, which harms Amazon’s marketplace integrity. ### **What You Should Do Instead of Reporting Immediately:** 1. **Leave a Neutral or Negative Review (If You Haven’t Yet)** - Since you didn’t actually leave a review, you could now leave an honest one (e.g., "Received a free item I didn’t earn, but the product was fine."). This exposes the seller’s deception without directly reporting them yet. - If you leave a **1-star review with a detailed explanation** (mentioning the fake review incentive), it could discourage others from falling for the same trick. 2. **Report the Seller to Amazon (But Strategically)** - If you decide to report them, use Amazon’s **Seller Feedback Report** (via Seller Central or the "Report Abuse" option on the listing). - **Be specific** in your report: - *"This seller offered a free item in exchange for a 5-star review, which violates Amazon’s review policy. I did not leave a review, but they still sent me a free item."* - Attach screenshots of their email correspondence and the printed note. 3. **Consider Reporting to Other Platforms (Optional)** - If you’re concerned about widespread deception, you could also report them to: - **Better Business Bureau (BBB)** – For deceptive business practices. - **East Asian Consumer Protection Agencies** (e.g., if you’re in South Korea, report to the [Korea Fair Trade Commission](https://www.ftckorea.go.kr/); in China, the [Cyberspace Administration](https://www.cac.gov.cn/)). - However, Amazon’s internal reporting is likely the most impactful. 4. **Warn Other Buyers (If You’re Comfortable)** - You could leave a comment on the seller’s listing (if allowed) or share the experience on forums like **Reddit (r/AmazonHelp)** or **Temu/Shein-related communities** (if applicable) to warn others. ### **Why Not Report Immediately?** - **Amazon’s Review System is Sensitive** – If you report a seller too quickly after receiving a free item, they might claim it was a "mistake" or "gift" rather than a violation. A well-timed review + report is stronger evidence. - **Some Sellers Get Away With It** – Amazon’s enforcement isn’t perfect, especially for long-standing sellers with high ratings. A detailed report + public exposure (via reviews) increases pressure. ### **Final Verdict:** **Yes, you’re justified in reporting them**, but **leaving a negative review first** (if you haven’t) and **reporting strategically** will have a bigger impact. This way, you’re not just punishing one seller but also protecting other buyers from their scheme. Would you like help drafting the exact wording for your review or report?
